transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Claire Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Gupta (Redwood SA), Jasmine Lee (Aurelius), Tom Becker (Aurelius), Priya Nair (Aurelius), Evan Cho (Aurelius)

Summary:
High level deep dive on Private VPC deployment options for Redwood's inference runtime. Focus on networking patterns: PrivateLink vs NAT egress, subnet sizing, DNS and route53 considerations, security (KMS/HSM, audit logs), and runtime performance impacts (latency/throughput, KV cache, batching, quantization). Agreed to run a 2-hour benchmark with KV-cache warmup and varied batching, and to exchange network diagrams and egress IPs.

Topics:
- PrivateLink endpoint + interface ENI approach vs NAT/IAM roles
- Egress and VPC firewall rules for model downloads, metrics, and control plane
- Subnet sizing for GPU nodes, ENI limits, IP exhaustion risk
- DNS resolution inside VPC and split-horizon / route53 private hosted zones
- Latency impacts of NAT/Proxy vs PrivateLink for inference RT requests
- KV cache warmup and stateful routing implications for private deployment
- Batching and quantization tradeoffs for predictable latency SLOs

Action items recap (quoted):
- Redwood to send network diagram and sample CloudFormation/terraform snippet for PrivateLink + VPC endpoints.
- SE to provide benchmark script and perf checklist.
- Aurelius to share firewall rules and egress requirements.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Claire Park: all right folks thanks for joining, um let's do intros quick, i'm claire redwood AE, and with me is mateo and nina from the se team, um and you all?
[00:08] Jasmine Lee: hey jasmine here, cloud architect at aurelius, tom and priya and evan are on as well.
[00:11] Tom Becker: hi everyone.
[00:13] Mateo Ruiz: great, quick agenda - we want to validate networking pattern for private vpc, cover private link vs nat, dns and subnet questions, and then talk about runtime perf implications like kv cache, batching, quantization. sound good?
[00:26] Jasmine Lee: yes that's perfect. we are evaluating private deploy because of PHI and residency concerns, and also want deterministic latency.
[00:34] Claire Park: totally. maybe quick context: redwood's private offering runs the inference runtime inside your VPC - control plane can be in our managed plane or also in customer control plane for private deployments - we support interface endpoints (privatelink), and a model where nodes egress via NAT for S3 model pulls - we'll walk the tradeoffs.
[00:52] Evan Cho: one immediate Q: we need to avoid public internet egress if possible for compliance. private link would be preferred but i've seen complexity with route53 and certs - can you explain how private link handles model downloads and runtime control traffic?
[01:07] Nina Gupta: yeah good question. with PrivateLink we create interface ENIs in your subnets for our control plane endpoints. model artifact downloads can be proxied over PrivateLink if you host artifacts on S3 with a VPC endpoint or via a presigned-url that your policy permits. otherwise, if you require full air-gap, we offer an on-prem package. note - some customers mirror models to an internal object store to avoid egress entirely.
[01:34] Priya Nair: and for KMS - will the runtime call out to our KMS or is there a managed key? we need envelope encryption and audit logs.
[01:41] Mateo Ruiz: you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS. The runtime supports calling your KMS endpoints over PrivateLink or VPC endpoints. Audit logs for inference requests and operator actions are pushed to your logging endpoint - we wire to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or to an on-prem syslog depending on setup. There was a small note - sometimes transcription: k-v cache is called kv cache or 'kayv' but it's the key-value past-token cache.
[02:08] Tom Becker: ok on the perf side: what's the latency delta if we use NAT egress for model calls versus a PrivateLink interface? we need p50 under 60ms for short prompts.
[02:19] Mateo Ruiz: depends on a few things. For inference RT requests coming from your application into the model runtime inside VPC, if you use PrivateLink to the control plane and traffic stays within region, then you avoid NAT traversal and hairpin - that keeps latency lower. NAT-based egress mainly affects model downloads and control plane callbacks; real-time inference requests typically route directly to the runtime inside VPC so latency impact is minimal. The bigger runtime impacts are batching, kv cache warm-up, and quantization choices.
[02:52] Jasmine Lee: can you explain kv cache warm-up? we've seen cold cache spikes.
[02:57] Nina Gupta: sure. the KV cache stores past key/value attention states for streaming or multi-turn chat. When a node hasn't seen a prefix, the first few requests need KV population, which can add ~10-30ms depending on sequence length. Redwood offers prefix caching and can pin conversational agents to warmed nodes for lower tail latency. For pilot, we'll run tests with a warmup load to measure p95.
[03:23] Tom Becker: and batching - our traffic pattern is bursty - so we worry batching will increase p50 or p95 unpredictably.
[03:30] Mateo Ruiz: batching is a tradeoff - throughput/cost vs latency. our runtime does continuous batching with latency SLO knobs: you can set max batch latency (e.g., 10ms) and a max batch size; the runtime will flush after the latency bound. For bursty traffic, we recommend sticky routing + small batch latency to keep p50 low and allow occasional batching to improve throughput. Also quantization - int8 can reduce token time significantly on some hardware but may slightly change output quality. we can run A/B with quantized model variants.
[04:02] Priya Nair: subnet sizing question - how many IPs per GPU node and ENIs do we need? evan is worried about hitting ec2 eni limits.
[04:10] Evan Cho: yes, our account has tight IPs.
[04:12] Nina Gupta: good point. GPU nodes typically need one primary ENI plus we create interface ENIs for PrivateLink endpoints; each interface consumes an IP. recommended pattern: allocate dedicated subnets per GPU pool, keep /24s for small pilots, scale to /22 for production depending on node counts. we also provide docs with ENI-to-instance type mapping; we'll send a terraform snippet that provisions endpoints in private subnets with security group rules minimal-allow.
[04:41] Jasmine Lee: about DNS - we use split-horizon route53 private hosted zones. if your control plane uses privatelink, will DNS resolve to the interface ip automatically?
[04:51] Mateo Ruiz: yes if you create the interface endpoint and choose to enable private DNS. Alternatively, you can use explicit CNAMEs to the vpce endpoint. There can be caching issues with negative responses; ensure your VPC resolver policies and TTLs are set low during cutover. Also, if you have custom DNS forwarding to an on-prem resolver, we recommend validating SRV records and ensure resolver has access to the endpoint.
[05:18] Tom Becker: one more - egress IPs. Our security team wants a narrow set of egress IPs for model pulls to whitelist in our storage provider. can you provide static IP ranges?
[05:26] Claire Park: for hosted control plane we publish a set of egress IPs per region; for PrivateLink + customer-managed control plane we can avoid egress by using VPC endpoints. For intermediate setups, we can publish a small pool and work with your security team to whitelist. we'll include that in the network diagram.
[05:44] Priya Nair: perf test plan - can you outline what you'd measure?
[05:48] Mateo Ruiz: yes - we'll measure cold vs warm KV cache, batch sizes (1,4,8), request sizes (short prompt vs long), quantization variants (fp16, int8), and p50/p95/p99 for token emit latencies and end-to-end. We'll also instrument token-level timings and KV cache hit rate. We'll share a test harness (python + locust style) and run a 2-hour window where we do warmup, steady-state, and a burst phase.
[06:18] Jasmine Lee: how does model rollout work in private? can you do canaries?
[06:22] Nina Gupta: yes, rollout and routing are configurable via the console or API. You can do percent-based canaries, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. For private deployments, the control plane signals the nodes; with PrivateLink you'll get low-latency control messages.
[06:37] Tom Becker: any gotchas for GPUs and quantization? we run A100 and some older V100s.
[06:42] Mateo Ruiz: A100s generally do very well with int8 and 4-bit mixed quant techniques; V100s have different kernel support and might degrade perf on some quant paths. We'll recommend a matrix for your fleet. Also, pinned CPU memory limits and NVLink configs matter for KV cache sizing - we'll include recommended instance types and kernel flags.
[07:05] Evan Cho: on firewall ports - what TCP ports need to be open for PrivateLink and runtime ops?
[07:10] Nina Gupta: primarily HTTPS (443) for control plane endpoints; we also use specific ports for metrics ingestion (configurable) and for internal node health-checking (they can be put on the SG). We'll send a minimal allow list.
[07:25] Jasmine Lee: one operational concern - if a node dies, how does state (KV cache) recovery affect tail latency?
[07:31] Mateo Ruiz: good question. if a node fails, requests routed to others will experience cold KV cache until warmed. We support sticky session routing for conversational agents and can pre-warm nodes during rollout. Also, we have fallback routing so low-tier nodes can serve in emergencies but with potentially higher latency.
[07:50] Claire Park: ok we're almost out of time. quick recap - we'll share network diagram, terraform/cloudformation snippets, a perf harness, and list of egress ips. Aurelius will validate firewall rules and confirm desired pilot node count.
[07:59] Jasmine Lee: perfect. expected timeline - can we aim to confirm pilot specs by next week?
[08:03] Claire Park: yes we'll follow up via email, set the benchmark window.
[08:05] Tom Becker: thanks everyone.
[08:07] Priya Nair: thanks.
